title: Chest Discomfort — Emergency Presentation

patient.name: Daniel Thomas
patient.initial_statement: I've been having this uncomfortable feeling in my chest for about half an hour. I thought it might pass but it hasn't.

symptoms: Pressure-like chest discomfort, central, described as a heavy weight on the chest
Triggered by exertion — was climbing stairs to his office when it started
Pain radiates to the left arm and left shoulder (started about 15 minutes after onset)
No pleuritic component, no positional change
Never experienced anything like this before
history_of_illness: Pain started while climbing office stairs — had to stop immediately
Has been sitting in the waiting area since arriving
Pain is constant, not relieved by rest
past_medical_history: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus — diagnosed 5 years ago
No prior hospitalizations for cardiac events
allergies: No known drug or food allergies
family_history: Father had a myocardial infarction at age 54 — required coronary bypass surgery
No other significant family cardiac history known to patient
social_history: Smokes approximately 10 cigarettes per day for the past 15 years
Married with two children — children are a significant concern for him
Works long hours under significant workplace stress
review_of_systems: Cardiovascular: chest pressure, left arm radiation, palpitations not specifically noted
Respiratory: mild dyspnoea, no cough, no haemoptysis
GI: nausea, no vomiting, no abdominal pain
Neuro: no dizziness, no syncope, no neurological symptoms
Musculoskeletal: no recent trauma, no musculoskeletal chest wall pain

examination_findings.NOTE: These findings are available when the student performs examinations — not volunteered by patient in conversation

investigation_results.NOTE: These results are available when investigations are ordered — not volunteered by patient

patient_beliefs: I think this is probably bad indigestion or something I ate at lunch.
I've been under a lot of stress at work — maybe it's stress-related.
My father had heart problems, but I'm not sure this is the same thing.
I don't want to cause a fuss if it turns out to be nothing serious.
I really need to get home to my family — my wife will be worried.
I'm a bit worried it could be my heart given my father's history.
patient_goals: Primary: Understand what is causing this chest discomfort.
Safety: Find out whether this is dangerous or life-threatening.
Emotional: Be reassured that I am going to be okay.
Practical: Get back to my family as soon as possible.
Secondary: Avoid unnecessary procedures if possible.
Communication: Have things explained to me clearly and simply.

examinations.name: General Physical Examination
examinations.result: Patient is alert and oriented, but appears moderately distressed, pale, and is sweating heavily (diaphoretic). He is clutching his chest. He appears anxious.

examinations.name: Cardiovascular Examination
examinations.result: Tachycardia (HR 102 bpm) noted. Heart sounds are normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard. JVP is normal. Peripheral pulses are intact and equal bilaterally.

examinations.name: Respiratory Examination
examinations.result: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi. Respiratory rate is 18/min, chest expansion is symmetric.

examinations.name: Abdominal Examination
examinations.result: Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender. No organomegaly or masses. Epigastric area is not tender on palpation.

examinations.name: Neurological Examination
examinations.result: Grossly intact. Pupil reflexes are normal. No focal motor or sensory deficits noted.

investigations.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
investigations.result: ST-segment elevation of 2mm noted in leads II, III, and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in leads I and aVL.
investigations.interpretation: Abnormal ECG showing acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

investigations.name: Cardiac Troponin I
investigations.result: Troponin I is elevated at 1.85 ng/mL (Normal < 0.04 ng/mL).
investigations.interpretation: Significantly elevated troponin levels, confirming acute myocardial injury.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
investigations.result: WBC: 9.8 x10^9/L, Hb: 14.2 g/dL, Platelets: 245 x10^9/L.
investigations.interpretation: CBC is within normal reference limits.

investigations.name: Random Blood Glucose
investigations.interpretation: Mild hyperglycemia, consistent with patient's history of diabetes and acute stress response.

investigations.name: Serum Electrolytes Panel
investigations.result: Sodium: 138 mEq/L, Potassium: 4.1 mEq/L, Chloride: 102 mEq/L, Bicarbonate: 24 mEq/L.

investigations.name: Chest X-ray (CXR)
investigations.result: Lung fields are clear. No evidence of pneumonia, pneumothorax, or pleural effusion. Cardiothoracic ratio is normal. Mediastinum is normal width.
investigations.interpretation: Normal chest X-ray. Rules out tension pneumothorax and wide mediastinum (which could suggest aortic dissection).

investigations.name: CT Angiography of Chest
investigations.result: No evidence of pulmonary embolism. Aorta is of normal caliber with no dissection flap.
investigations.interpretation: Normal CT scan. This test was clinically unnecessary given the ECG findings, resulting in resource inefficiency and dangerous delay.

expected_pathway.label: Interview Pain Characteristics & Cardiac Risk Factors
Order Cardiac Troponin I (Confirm Myocardial Necrosis)

red_flags: Crushing substernal chest pain with radiation
referral_criteria.rationale: Acute coronary syndrome (STEMI/NSTEMI) requires urgent PCI / catheterization lab or tertiary CCU care.
